title: The product that half published
blurb: Per-field swaps and best-effort renditions tore the page.
prompt: Shoppers saw a new price with the old description for a full hour, and one SKU published without its main image because the draft treated renditions as best-effort. The model-generated draft swaps fields into a shared hash. Review it, fix it, and prove publishing is atomic and all-or-nothing.
aiNote: The draft applies publish changes field by field into the shared catalog hash, so readers observe a product assembled from two versions, and it declares publish success when one rendition lands, leaving the storefront with missing media.
testIdea: Swap a price and title concurrently and read repeatedly to assert every read shows one full version; fail the main rendition and assert the publish is held back; inspect storefront responses for draft fields.
followUps: How do you preview a draft to the right audience?
What cache-control pattern keeps CDNs from mixing versions?
When should a rollback re-publish an old version versus unreleasing it?
